Terms of Use

Effective November 25, 2026 · Version 2.0 · Previous versions

bloop is a new, free side project, not a commercial service, and may change. Accounts are by invite, for adults. Your files stay yours: bloop stores them in the EU, uses them only to show them where you choose, and deletes them when you say. Show only files you have the right to show; bloop may remove a file or suspend an Account that breaks these terms, and you can appeal. The law of England and Wales applies.

1 Who Runs bloop

Summary, not binding: In short: bloop is run by one person in the UK.

1.1 bloop is run by Duke DJ Saputra, an individual based in the United Kingdom ("bloop"), as a free side project in early access. Contact: hi@bloop.here; a postal address is available on request.

1.2 These Terms apply to anyone who uses bloop at bloop.here, with or without an Account, including the Demo ("you"). The words Account, Library, Screen, Session, Item, Guest File and Demo mean what they mean in the Privacy Notice, section 1.4.

1.3 By using bloop, you accept these Terms. If you do not accept them, do not use bloop.

2 What bloop Is Today

Summary, not binding: In short: a free early version that may change or stop.

2.1 bloop is in early access. It is free, and some features are not built yet: see what works today.

2.2 bloop is not a commercial service: nothing is sold, charged or paid for, and no contract for payment arises from using it.

2.3 These Terms are between you and bloop. Using bloop for your job does not commit your organization to anything.

3 Your Account

Summary, not binding: In short: one invite, one adult, one email; keep your phone and email safe.

3.1 Accounts are by invite only. An invite is for the one email address it was sent to, works once, and expires after 7 days. You may not pass it on.

3.2 You must be 18 or over to have an Account. By opening one, you confirm that you are.

3.3 You sign in with a code sent to your email, or a passkey on your device. Anyone who can read your email can sign in as you, so keep your email account secure, and sign out everywhere from Account if you lose a device.

3.4 Keep your phone locked. Anyone holding your unlocked, signed-in phone can act as you.

3.5 Check that the number on your phone matches the Screen before you approve. End a Session when you are done; it also ends by itself when the time shown on your phone runs out.

3.6 When file services are live, you may connect only an account you have the right to use, and you are responsible for following your organization's rules about it.

4 Your Library

Summary, not binding: In short: 5 GB of space, files up to 500 MB, a 30-day Trash, and a warning before an unused Account is deleted.

4.1 Each Account can store up to 5 GB of files, and each file can be up to 500 MB. Files in your Trash count toward the 5 GB until they are deleted for good; the copies bloop makes to show your files do not.

4.2 A file you delete goes to your Trash for 30 days, where you can restore it. After that, or when you empty it from the Trash, it is deleted for good and cannot be recovered.

4.3 If you do not use your Account for 12 months, bloop emails you a warning. If you do not sign in within 30 days of that email, bloop deletes your Account and everything in it.

4.4 You can download a copy of your files and your data at any time with Export in Account.

4.5 You can delete your Account at any time with Delete Account in Account. It is deleted 7 days later, with everything in it; sign in before then to cancel. What bloop keeps after that, and why: the Privacy Notice.

4.6 bloop is not a backup service. Keep your own copy of anything you cannot afford to lose.

5 Acceptable Use

Summary, not binding: In short: nothing unlawful, harmful or abusive, and no attacks on the service.

5.1 You must not use bloop to show, send or store anything that:

  1. (a) is unlawful, or that you do not have the right to share;
  2. (b) is abusive, harassing, hateful, threatening or sexually explicit;
  3. (c) shows or promotes child sexual abuse, terrorism, or intimate images of anyone without their consent;
  4. (d) contains malware, macros or other active content.

5.2 You must not:

  1. (a) put content on a Screen you are not in front of, or claim a Screen someone else is using;
  2. (b) use bloop as storage for files you do not mean to present, or to give other people access to files;
  3. (c) probe, scan or test bloop's security except as the disclosure policy allows;
  4. (d) overload, scrape or automate bloop, or get around its limits;
  5. (e) share your Account, or resell bloop or offer it as part of another service.

6 Your Content

Summary, not binding: In short: your files stay yours; bloop may use them only to run the service for you.

6.1 bloop claims no ownership of your files, links or Guest Files.

6.2 You give bloop a limited, non-exclusive, free license to store, copy, check and convert your files, and to show them on the Screens you choose, only as needed to provide bloop to you: keeping them in your Library, making the copies used to show them, sending them to the Screens you approve, and including them in your Export. bloop may not use your files for anything else: not to train software, not to advertise, and not to show to anyone you did not choose.

6.3 The license ends for a file when it is deleted for good, and for everything when your Account is deleted, except for any copy the law requires bloop to keep (the Privacy Notice).

6.4 You confirm that you have the right to store and show each file you upload, and that it follows section 5.

7 Guest Files

Summary, not binding: In short: you are responsible for what you send; bloop shows it during the Session, then deletes it.

7.1 If you send a Guest File, you confirm that you have the right to show it and that it follows section 5.

7.2 You give bloop a limited license to store, check, convert and show the Guest File on the Screen you chose, only until the Session ends. bloop then deletes it, unless the law requires bloop to keep it (how long).

7.3 bloop's checks refuse some files, such as decks with macros.

8 Reports, Removal and Suspension

Summary, not binding: In short: anyone can report a file; bloop can disable files and suspend Accounts, and tells you why.

8.1 To report illegal content or a file that breaks these Terms, use Report on the Screen or at bloop.here/report, or email hi@bloop.here with "Report" in the subject, saying what, where and when. If the file is still on a Screen, anyone at the Screen can remove it at once by pressing End.

8.2 bloop reviews every report without undue delay, and removes or disables illegal content as soon as it knows of it. A disabled file can no longer be shown, previewed or exported by anyone.

  1. (a) If the report is about an intimate image of you shared without your consent, bloop removes it within 48 hours of your report at the latest.
  2. (b) If you think a file shows child sexual abuse, do not download, copy or forward it. Tell bloop, which reports it to the National Crime Agency as the law requires. If a child is in danger now, call 999.

8.3 bloop may refuse, disable or delete any file, and may stop Guest Files for everyone for a time, to keep the service safe or lawful.

8.4 bloop may suspend your Account if you break these Terms, if a report about your files needs looking into, or if needed to keep the service or others safe. While suspended, you cannot sign in to present or upload, and your sign-ins end. bloop may close your Account for a serious or repeated breach, such as sharing illegal content.

8.5 When bloop disables your file or suspends or closes your Account, it emails you what it did, which part of these Terms it relied on, and how to appeal, unless the law or a police investigation stops it from saying so. You can still ask for a copy of your data (your rights), except for content the law requires bloop to hold back.

8.6 How bloop protects people from illegal content: Accounts are by invite only, for adults, each tied to one email; a Guest File never opens by itself, so someone at the Screen must click Open; files reach a Screen only through links made for that Session, which expire, so no one can pass a file on through bloop; bloop's checks refuse files that are not what they claim to be and files with macros or embedded programs; and bloop acts on reports under 8.2. bloop does not scan the contents of files.

9 Complaints and Appeals

Summary, not binding: In short: tell bloop if you think it got a decision wrong; it looks again and tells you why.

9.1 You can complain or appeal if bloop disabled, refused or deleted your file, suspended or closed your Account, did not act on your report, or did not follow these Terms on illegal content. Email hi@bloop.here with "Appeal" or "Complaint" in the subject, saying what happened and why you think it is wrong, within 6 months of the decision.

9.2 bloop acknowledges it within 5 working days, looks at the decision again from the start with what you send, and tells you the outcome and why within 14 days where it can. bloop is run by one person, so that person reviews it again; you can ask for a note of the reasons. If bloop got it wrong, it reverses the decision, restores what it can, and says so.

9.3 This does not affect your right to go to court, or to complain to Ofcom about how bloop handles illegal content in general.

10 Availability

Summary, not binding: In short: offered as it is, with no promise of uptime.

10.1 bloop is offered "as is" during early access, with no promise that it will always be available or free of errors. Keep another way to present, such as a copy on a laptop or USB drive.

10.2 bloop may change, pause or end the service. bloop will try to give 30 days' notice by email before ending it, so you can export your files.

10.3 A Screen gets a link to each Item, and those links stop working when the Session ends. A downloaded copy or the PC's history can stay on the PC until it is wiped: see what can stay.

11 Liability

Summary, not binding: In short: the law's protections stay; beyond them, bloop's liability is small while bloop is free.

11.1 Nothing in these Terms limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for anything else the law does not allow to be limited.

11.2 Subject to 11.1, bloop is not liable for any lost data or for any indirect or consequential loss.

11.3 Subject to 11.1, bloop's total liability to you for everything arising from your use of bloop is limited to £100, because bloop is a free service.

11.4 Nothing in these Terms takes away any right the law gives you that cannot be excluded.

12 Ending Access

Summary, not binding: In short: you can leave any time; bloop can end Accounts that break these Terms.

12.1 You can stop using bloop at any time, and delete your Account as 4.5 describes.

12.2 bloop may end your access as section 8 describes. If bloop ends the service, or ends your Account for a reason other than a breach of these Terms, it will give you a chance to export your files first where it can.

13 Changes to These Terms

Summary, not binding: In short: dated changes, with notice for big ones.

13.1 bloop may change these Terms. A change gets a new version and date here. For a material change, bloop will post it here and give 30 days' notice where it can by email to Account holders and the waitlist. Using bloop after a change takes effect means you accept it; if you do not, you can export your files and delete your Account.

Summary, not binding: In short: English law; your local UK courts still apply if you live elsewhere in the UK.

14.1 These Terms are governed by the law of England and Wales, and its courts have jurisdiction. If you live in Scotland or Northern Ireland, you may also bring a claim in your local courts, and any mandatory protection where you live still applies.
